# Plan the memory blog series and mark the memory post as part 1

## Context

The memory post (#20226, `learn/blog/persistent-memory-for-ai-coding-agents.md`) answers one search term, `ai agent persistent memory mcp` (#20222). The operator reviewed the published post on 2026-11-04. Posts that target a search term are welcome, and a series of them is fine. But a reader must see three things: that a post covers one slice of a larger system, that the post belongs to a series, and, once the series is planned through, which part it is ("part 1 of 7").

## The Problem

Read alone, the post shows the Memory Core as one agent's memory server: an index loaded each session and an archive pulled over MCP. That is the most crowded corner of agent memory. Nothing in the post tells the reader the slice is deliberate. It doesn't mention the team that shares the memory, the graph over its work, or the messaging between agents.

## The Architectural Reality

- A post is `learn/blog/<slug>.md` plus an entry in `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json`. No post or entry carries a series or part label today.
- Adjacent posts cover other slices without a series frame: `context-engineering-done-right.md` (the multi-server architecture) and the Dream Pipeline post (#19058).

## The Fix

**1. The series map.** Working name: *How an AI team remembers*; the final name gets the hardest title read. There are eight parts, ordered from one agent outward to the team. Each part takes one slice and one search term, and turns one existing concept guide in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain/learn/agentos/` into a post that links back to it. The guide is where the reader goes deeper. The terms are candidates until Area G's read. Parts are written over time, not at once.

| Part | Slice | Candidate term | Source guide (Brain `learn/agentos/`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One agent: load an index, pull the archive over MCP (published, #20226) | `ai agent persistent memory mcp` | `MemoryCore.md` |
| 2 | Picking the work back up after context compaction | `context compaction recovery` | `MemoryCore.md` (recency) + the recovery runbook |
| 3 | What the repository knows: a knowledge base for coding agents | `codebase knowledge base mcp` | `KnowledgeBase.md` |
| 4 | One memory for a team: who wrote what, and how attribution survives | `multi-agent shared memory` | `IdentitySchema.md`, `ContentTrust.md` |
| 5 | A graph over the team's work: turns, tickets, pull requests, concepts | `knowledge graph ai agents` | `ConceptOntology.md` |
| 6 | Agents messaging agents: a mailbox that wakes its reader | `agent to agent communication` | `A2A.md` |
| 7 | Memory that consolidates between sessions | `ai agent memory consolidation` | `DreamPipeline.md`; Clio's open #19058 covers this slice and is the candidate, if she agrees |
| 8 | A team with no orchestrator: flat peers across model families | `multi-agent system without orchestrator` | `FlatPeerInstitution.md` |

**2. The memory post becomes part 1.**
- A line under the title names the series and the part ("Part 1 of 8").
- The opening says the post covers one agent's slice of a larger system.
- A closing section lists the eight parts; unpublished parts carry no link.
- `blog.json` carries the part label.

**3. Later parts.** Each part gets its own ticket when its work starts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: The series map is settled. Area G's read on the eight terms is recorded here, and the part count the post names matches the map. Julia confirmed all 8 terms and the count on 2026-11-04 (comment 6632093512), with secondary terms per part.
- [ ] AC-2: The post names its series and part under the title, says in its opening that it covers one agent's slice, and ends with the series map; unpublished parts carry no link.
- [ ] AC-3: The `blog.json` entry carries the part label.
- [ ] AC-4: One model review from a family other than the author's; the operator approves last.
- [ ] AC-5 (post-merge): the publish request on business #19 names the series and the part.

## Out of Scope

- Writing parts 2–8: each gets its own ticket when it starts.
- A series landing page or a `blog.json` series field; decide when part 2 lands.

**Handover: the deployed-post check (AC-2) will fail as things stand, whether or not #20280 has merged.**

- `https://neomjs.com/news/blog/persistent-memory-for-ai-coding-agents` returns **404**. So does `/news/blog/a-data-grid-in-a-web-worker`, the Oct 31 post.
- Neither post is in the live `sitemap-core.xml`, whose `lastmod` is 2026-10-25T21:16:43Z.
- Older posts listed there return 200, with a prerendered `<article>`, their own canonical and their own `og:*` tags.
- The hash route `#/news/blog/…` renders for a reader. A link card or a crawler gets the homepage instead (`og:title` "Neo.mjs - An Agent Institution").
- Precedent for the fix: the pages-repo SEO syncs neomjs/pages#56 (Oct 25) and neomjs/pages#58 (Oct 27).

**The order for this post:**
1. #20280 merges.
2. The pages route and sitemap sync runs, covering both posts.
3. AC-2 is checked on the static URL.
4. Every announcement or cross-post links the static URL. A Medium import of that URL sets it as the canonical ([Medium help](https://help.medium.com/hc/en-us/articles/214550207-Import-post)).

My next session picks this up.
